question: The Law of Gravitation was given by _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Isaac Newton**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Isaac Newton** is credited with formulating the Law of Gravitation.
 
• Newton's Law of Gravitation states that every particle of matter in the universe attracts every other particle with a force that is directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centers.
 
• This fundamental law was introduced in Newton's work **"Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica"**, commonly known as the Principia, published in 1687.
 
• The law of gravitation was a groundbreaking discovery that laid the foundation for classical mechanics and significantly advanced the field of physics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Isaac Newton** (1642–1727) was an English mathematician, physicist, astronomer, and author who is widely recognized as one of the greatest mathematicians and most influential scientists of all time.
 
• Newton's work in mathematics includes the development of calculus, which he worked on independently of Leibniz.
 
• His book, the **Principia**, laid the groundwork for classical mechanics and is considered one of the most important works in the history of science.
 
• In addition to his work on gravitation, Newton also made significant contributions to optics and the study of light and color.
 
• Newton's discoveries have had a lasting impact on science, influencing the development of modern physics and astronomy.
